slides.texte_overlay:
Timeless manners that make
you impossible to forget
Replying to invitations quickly. Yes or no within a day, never a vague "maybe." Hosts remember the guest who made planning easy, and they invite him again.
Bringing the conversation back to the quiet person. "Lena, you went there last year, right?" Including people who struggle to speak up is a mark of real class.
Arriving with something for the host. Flowers, a dessert, a good bottle. Never arrive empty-handed. It's a simple tradition that people still deeply appreciate.
Knowing a little about the world. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and being able to talk about many things is an old-fashioned charm people love.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Being able to talk about many things is a charm people still love.

slides.texte_overlay: Offering your seat. On the bus, in a waiting room, at a crowded bar. Giving up your seat without a fuss is old school kindness that people remember for a long time.
Asking before you take the last of anything. The last slice of pizza, the last drink. "Does anyone want this?" shows you think of others first, even in small things.
Thanking people by name and in person. Not just in a text. Looking someone in the eye and saying "Thank you, Sarah, that meant a lot" is something they keep.
